questions.question: I. Definition of biological species was given by Ernst Mayr. II. Photoperiod does not affect reproduction in plants. III. Binomial nomenclature system was given by RH Whittaker. IV. In unicellular organisms, reproduction is synonymous with growth. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.questionHtml:
I. Definition of biological species was given by Ernst Mayr.

II. Photoperiod does not affect reproduction in plants.

III. Binomial nomenclature system was given by RH Whittaker.

IV. In unicellular organisms, reproduction is synonymous with growth.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
I. True: The definition of biological species was indeed given by Ernst Mayr. He defined a species as a group of interbreeding natural populations that are reproductively isolated from other such groups.

II. False: Photoperiod does affect reproduction in plants. The length of day and night can influence flowering and other reproductive processes in many plants.

III. False: The binomial nomenclature system was introduced by Carl Linnaeus, not RH Whittaker. Linnaeus is known as the father of modern taxonomy.

IV. True: In unicellular organisms, reproduction is synonymous with growth. For example, when a unicellular organism like bacteria divides, it results in two new cells, which can be considered as both growth and reproduction.
